Subject: Realtime chat seeing 5-9s p99 during peak — need urgent help

Hi Karthik,

We're seeing a sharp rise in p99 latency on the realtime streaming socket endpoint (SSE/WebSocket) during our evening peak window (roughly 18:00-19:30 PDT). p95 is elevated too (~1.2s -> ~2.4s) but p99 is spiking into 5-9s territory intermittently and some messages are timing out entirely. Attached is a small log excerpt and a screenshot of our metrics.

Attachments: quikchat_p99_excerpt.log, pre_mitigation_p99_dashboard.png

Quick triage notes (what I can see from infra right now):
- Observed a sudden rise in request queue depth across the websocket worker pool serving QuikChat in us-west-2 starting 2028-07-12T22:58:00Z.
- Kernel-level metrics show GPU utilization at ~95% on several hosts and token-generation stalls coincident with long tail. KV cache hit rate dipped (~18% -> 9%) during the spike (likely cache churn due to burst of distinct sessions).
- No recent model rollout in that pool in the last 48h; no obvious deployment flag changed in the canary history.

Suggested immediate mitigations (will act now if approved):
1) Enable autoscale burst for the QuikChat route (adds ephemeral nodes to reduce queue depth) — low-risk, will increase spend.
2) Temporarily lower per-instance max-connections (reduce queueing) and rely on routing to scale horizontally.
3) If burst doesn't reduce p99 in 10m, failover the route to the backup region canary in us-west-1 (we have spare capacity there).

I've opened SUP-2345 and uploaded a netdiag bundle to the ticket. Applying step 1 now; will update in 7-10m with p99 numbers.

Attachments: netdiag_bundle_20280712.txt

—Sean
